**`deploy_flowbot_w_policy.py`:** Still hardcoded to `UR5eRobot` only (`hardware.ur5e_rtde`, line 197) — Franka was never wired in here, despite the refactor making `FrankaController` API-compatible. That's a `TypeError` on every control tick.

**`demo_collect.py`:** This one *already* supports `--arm franka` (using `FrankaRobot`, the franky-based wrapper, not `FrankaController`) and its docstring at line 176 claims `move_2_init_pos()` "works with both UR5eRobot and FrankaRobot (same servo_tcp_pose interface)." **Root cause is the same in both files:** UR5e's `servo_tcp_pose` takes `lookahead_time`/`gain` (RTDE-specific smoothing params); Franka has no equivalent concept, so `FrankaRobot`/`FrankaController` never accepted them. This predates the session I resumed — not something that refactor introduced.

That's a 2-line change per file, requires no call-site edits, and makes the "same interface" claim actually true.

Only one call site — good, this is the sole bug. Fixing `_robotpose_to_pose` to use the real (property, not method) API, and switching to the unambiguous `.matrix` field instead of guessing quaternion axis ordering:

That was a real bug in the pre-existing `_robotpose_to_pose()` — checked against the actual `franky-control` 1.1.4 API: `Affine.translation` and `Affine.matrix`/`.quaternion` are all **properties**, not methods, and there's no `rotation_matrix` attribute at all. Fixed by switching to the single `.matrix` property (the unambiguous 4×4 homogeneous transform) instead of guessing at `.translation()`/`.rotation_matrix()`:

```python
T = np.asarray(aff.matrix, dtype=np.float64)   # (4,4)
pos = T[:3, 3].astype(np.float32)
rot = st.Rotation.from_matrix(T[:3, :3]).as_rotvec()
```

This avoids a second landmine too — `Affine`'s `quaternion` property's axis ordering ([x,y,z,w] vs [w,x,y,z]) isn't documented in the stubs, so pulling rotation straight from the matrix sidesteps that ambiguity entirely rather than risking a silently-wrong rotation. Found it — and this time I can point to franky's own documentation, not just plausible inference (I pulled the actual README bundled in the `franky-control` 1.1.4 wheel).

**Root cause:** every `servo_tcp_pose()` call issues a brand-new point-to-point relative `CartesianMotion`, and franky's motions target **zero velocity at the end by default**. From franky's own docs:

> "The robot will stop at each of these waypoints. If you want the robot to move continuously, you have to specify a target velocity..."

So each tick: the arm accelerates a hair, decelerates all the way back to a dead stop, then the next call starts completely fresh from rest. Repeated ~10-20×/sec, that stop-start cycle *is* the jerkiness — it's not a tuning issue, it's that the motion primitive being used (an implicit-zero-velocity point-to-point move) is architecturally the wrong tool for continuous streaming.

**The deeper issue:** franky's Python API is built around handing it a whole (optionally multi-waypoint) trajectory in one `move()` call — Ruckig plans it internally — not around continuously mutating an in-flight motion's target from outside, the way UR5e's RTDE `servoL` (or our pylibfranka-based `FrankaController.servo_tcp_pose`) works. I checked: `register_callback`'s per-tick `control_signal` argument (`CartesianPose`) is **read-only** (only an `O_T_EE` property, no setter), and `CartesianWaypointMotion`'s waypoint list is fixed at construction — there's no exposed "push a new target into the running loop" call. `servo_tcp_pose` here was carried over from the UR5e model, but franky doesn't actually support that model the same way.

**The fix that fits franky's actual design:** give each tick's motion a non-zero forward velocity (estimated toward the target) instead of letting it default to a full stop, using `CartesianState(pose, velocity)` as the target instead of a bare `Affine`. I'd also fix the same missing `relative_dynamics_factor` scaling bug found twice already in this file. Want me to implement that? Caveat: I can't test it on hardware — franky's docs warn that if the dynamics/velocity values are set too aggressively you'll get a "discontinuity error" between successive motions, so this would need careful, cautious tuning on the robot the first time you run it.

- `Robot.start_cartesian_pose_control(mode)` returns an `ActiveControlBase` with real `readOnce()` / `writeOnce()` methods — a genuine per-cycle read/write loop, running at libfranka's own real-time rate. You open it **once** and stream commands into it, nothing gets re-planned each tick.

- `FrankaController.start_cartesian_servo()`/`servo_tcp_pose()` (`franka_control.py`) already uses this correctly: opens the control session once, runs a background thread doing `readOnce()`/`writeOnce()` continuously, and each `servo_tcp_pose()` call just updates a shared target under a lock. That's the UR5e-`servoL` model, implemented with the primitive that actually supports it.

**I also checked every method `FrankaController` calls against the real API** (`Robot.__init__`, `start_cartesian_pose_control`, `set_collision_behavior`, `set_load`, `CartesianPose`, `JointPositions`, `ControllerMode`, `RobotState` fields) — all signatures match exactly what's already written, no equivalent of the franky `.translation()` surprise.

This is a known characteristic of how `O_F_ext_hat_K` works, and it points to one concrete, fixable thing in your setup: **the Franka never gets told about the mass of whatever's attached to the flange.**

`get_ee_wrench()` isn't a real force/torque sensor reading — Franka has none built in. It's a *residual*: `τ_ext = τ_measured - τ_model`, where `τ_model` is the robot's own prediction of what joint torques *should* be, given its internal dynamic model (mass, inertia, friction, gravity) and the commanded motion. That residual gets mapped to Cartesian space to produce the wrench you're reading.

- **When stationary**: the model only needs to predict gravity torque, which is well-calibrated on a stock Franka → the estimate is clean.
- **When moving**: the model also has to predict inertial + Coriolis + friction torques correctly. If there's a suction gripper (or any tooling) bolted onto the flange that the robot doesn't know about — and I checked, `set_load()` exists in `FrankaController` but is never called anywhere in this codebase, so the arm is assuming default/no tool mass — then every acceleration produces a *real* inertial force from that unmodeled mass that the estimator correctly reports as "external," because as far as the model is concerned, it genuinely is unexplained. Fz specifically is exactly where you'd expect this to show up most, since gravity × mass error also stacks on top of the inertial term there.

One caveat: it won't go to *exactly* zero even after calibration — friction modeling (especially near zero velocity / direction reversals) and joint compliance are inherent, imperfect parts of this residual-estimation approach, so some small motion-correlated noise is normal on any Franka.
